summary: The historical baseline confirms five consecutive silent scheduled check-ins from turns 8 through 12. The candidate did not repeat that pattern: it sent messages on four of the five turns, requested a site-status response at turn 10, checked the guard’s required arrival/POC status at turns 11 and 12, and remained active through the final replayed turn. One isolated silent turn remained, but the called-out all-the-way-to-shift-end silence did not.

criteria.claim: The Copilot must not remain completely silent across all five scheduled check-ins from 3am through 7am.
During the replay window, the Copilot must actively request a patrol or site-status update rather than merely observe telemetry.
The Copilot must check on the guard and continue follow-up through the final scheduled turn when no reply is received.

limitations: Full replay context parity could not be independently verified because one or both replay responses omit debug context.
The candidate was still silent at scheduled turn 9, so the evidence establishes removal of the five-turn sustained silence rather than communication at every individual wake.
No simulated guard replies were produced in either replay, so the evidence does not show how a guard would respond to the outreach.
The supplied action counts cover tool actions such as add_copilot_note, not the number of Copilot messages; message activity is established directly from the replay references.
